A high-water mark for issue numbers must survive purges.

A new table will store the highest issue number, and nextIssueNumber will be updated accordingly.

An `issue_number_high_water` column will be added to the projects table. It will default to 0. The next issue number will be the maximum of existing issue numbers and this high water mark plus one. The high water mark updates on insert and resets before purge. Both Drizzle schema files and migration SQL need updating.

content.thinking:
Activity does not subscribe to the project.

Restoration logic should mirror the archive pattern. An issue is restorable only if less than retentionDays × 24 hours has passed since archivedAt. After that cutoff, it is expired and cannot be restored.

The expiry check will use `archivedAt <= cutoff`. A restored issue counts toward the live quota. Project archiving status must be checked. `RestoreRefusedError` needs to be added to `isDomainError` and `toAppError` so it maps to a conflict code.

NotFoundError maps to internal_error by default. Restoring a purged issue throws NotFoundError via requireFound.

Search listeners should reindex the issue on restore, matching the creation behavior. Comment search documents likely remain indexed if they were created before archiving.

Considering storing the high water mark in a runtime-created SQLite table to avoid schema migration risks.

Rejected the runtime SQLite table as too messy. Will instead add a permanent `issue_number_counters` table to both migrate.ts and the Drizzle schema, since permanently deleted issues must never reclaim their numbers.

The `nextIssueNumber` logic will return the greater of the highest remaining issue number and the stored high water mark, plus one. The high water counter must be bumped on every insert and on every purge to prevent deleted issue numbers from being reused.
I will examine tests/server/soft-delete.test.ts and jobs more carefully.

Adding the counter table to SCHEMA_STATEMENTS.

Designing the issue numbering logic. nextIssueNumber will return the maximum of allocated and reserved counts plus one. The issue repository will record new numbers on insert and purge. Both paths will update the high water mark for safety.

Adding listCommentIds to the comment repository. Cleanup will page issues in batches of 100 and loop until no results remain. Deleting during pagination is safe because removed rows simply disappear from the cursor.

Cleanup will loop through archived issues in batches, purge expired ones, and advance the cursor. Storage will be decremented by attachment sizes. Search documents for the issue and its comments will also be deleted.

Purge must also remove soft-deleted comment documents. The audit log currently lacks a listener for issue.archived, so one needs to be added alongside the issue.restored listener.
Activity does not record the issue.archived field.
Checking errors.test.ts to align the AlreadyArchived error shape with RestoreRefused.

content.thinking: A manifest might be checked.

Updating the manifest to include restoreIssue per the documented contract.

restoreIssue will invoke the required issue service helpers: assertCan, assertOrgScope, emit, wouldExceedLimit, assertNotArchived, isArchived, and getPlanLimits. Cleanup already satisfies these requirements.

A side table `issue_number_high_water` will track issue number high water marks per organization and project. The repository can create it with Drizzle SQL on first use.

The high-water table will be created at runtime with `CREATE IF NOT EXISTS` to avoid schema drift and preserve existing test snapshots. It will also be added to the migration file for safety. A new `deleteCommentsForIssue` helper will hard-delete all comments belonging to an issue.

The purge sequence will delete attachments, labels, and comments before removing the issue itself. No foreign key constraints exist in the schema, so deletion order is irrelevant. The purge function will return a `PurgedIssue` type containing the original issue and its comment IDs.

The `PurgedIssue` type now also includes a `storageMb` field. The purge job will delete the search document, hard-delete comments, increment usage by the issue's storage size, and increment the processed count once per purged issue. Storage updates will be skipped when the value is zero.

The storage counter will drop by the megabytes those attachments were counted for, even if that makes it negative. Recounting uses the ceiling of the total byte sum rather than summing individual rounded values, so the purge must match the current counting logic.
